question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

At gurukul they spend many years together, growing into the best of friends, and ______ was time for each to return to his home, they wept.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. when it.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank must join the two ideas — living together as friends and weeping — by showing the time at which the second event happened, so a conjunction of time is required.

◦ "When" is the subordinating conjunction that introduces a time clause, and the impersonal subject "it" is needed with the expression "it was time (for somebody) to do something".

◦ Correct: ... growing into the best of friends, and when it was time for each to return to his home, they wept.

◦ Structure to remember: It is / was time + for + object + to-infinitive — It was time for us to leave.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "instantly it" and Option 2 "soon it" are adverbs, not conjunctions, and cannot introduce the clause here.

• Option 4 "after it" would place the weeping before the departure time and breaks the natural sequence of events described.

NOTE

• Common conjunctions of time: when, while, before, after, as soon as, till, until, since, whenever.

• The word "gurukul" refers to the ancient Indian residential schooling system, where pupils lived at the teacher's home — useful background for comprehension passages.

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

The television is big, has an excellent picture, and last but not ______ , it's cheap.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. least.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed idiomatic expression is "last but not least", used when mentioning the final item in a list, to make clear that it is no less important than the others.

◦ Correct: The television is big, has an excellent picture, and last but not least, it's cheap.

◦ Here the speaker lists three merits of the television, and the cheap price — mentioned last — is presented as equally important.

◦ "Least" is the superlative of little, so the phrase literally means "last in order but not the smallest in importance".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "close", 2 "final" and 3 "end" all suggest an ending, but none of them completes this set phrase, which cannot be altered.

• Idioms are fixed expressions: changing even one word makes them wrong.

NOTE

• Other useful list-ordering expressions: first of all, to begin with, moreover, furthermore, in addition, finally, last but not least.

• Degrees of little: little – less – least; of much/many: much/many – more – most.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Go down like a lead balloon
option_1: To be received badly by an audience
option_2: Put yourself in a tough position in order to support someone / something
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. To be received badly by an audience.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "go down like a lead balloon" means to be received very badly; to fail completely to impress or amuse people. (बुरी तरह नाकाम होना)

◦ Example: His joke about the manager went down like a lead balloon at the office party.

◦ Origin: a balloon made of lead would be far too heavy to float — it would simply drop to the ground, exactly like a speech or joke that falls flat.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 describes the idiom to go out on a limb (to take a risk to support someone).

• Option 3 "Surrender peacefully" corresponds to throw in the towel or lay down one's arms.

• Option 4 "To gamble everything you have" is to put all one's eggs in one basket or to go for broke.

NOTE

• Related idioms of failure: fall flat, bomb, come a cropper, go up in smoke, bite the dust.

• The opposite idea — being very well received — is expressed by go down a treat or bring the house down.

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

One appointed to act in place of another
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Deputy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Deputy" is a person appointed to act in place of, or as an assistant to, another person, especially in that person's absence. (उप / प्रतिनिधि)

◦ The word comes from the French deputer, meaning to appoint.

◦ Examples: Deputy Commissioner, Deputy Speaker, Deputy Chief Minister — each acts on behalf of the principal officer.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Minister" = a member of the government in charge of a department; the post is not defined by acting in someone's place.

• Option 3 "Officer" = a person holding a position of authority, a very general term.

• Option 4 "Delegate" = a person sent to represent a group at a conference or meeting; the stress is on representation at an event, not on standing in for one individual.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutions: proxy (a person authorised to act for another, especially in voting), surrogate (a substitute), locum (a temporary stand-in for a doctor or priest), regent (one who rules on behalf of a monarch).

• Word family: depute (verb), deputation (noun), deputy (noun/adjective).

question:
Select the word from the options which is exactly opposite in meaning to the bracketed word given in the sentence below.

It automatically (adjusts) resistance to match the road grade.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. disorganise.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Adjust" means to alter or set something slightly so that it fits, works better or suits a purpose; to arrange properly. (समायोजित करना)

◦ Its opposite must convey throwing into disorder / upsetting a proper arrangement, and "disorganise" means exactly that — to destroy the order or system of something. (अव्यवस्थित करना)

◦ In the sentence the machine sets the resistance correctly; the opposite would be to disturb that setting.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "rectify" = to put right or correct — a synonym in spirit, not an antonym.

• Option 2 "order" = to arrange systematically — again close in sense to 'adjust'.

• Option 3 "suit" = to be convenient or acceptable to — related to fitting, so not opposite.

NOTE

• Synonyms of adjust: adapt, modify, regulate, set, fine-tune, accommodate.

• Antonyms of adjust: disorganise, derange, disarrange, upset, disturb.

• The prefix dis- reverses meaning: disorganise, disagree, disconnect, dishonest, disobey.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

After recess, the students returns to their desks.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. returned to their.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Two points decide this question — subject–verb agreement and the correct spelling of the possessive.

◦ The subject "the students" is plural, so the singular verb "returns" is wrong; the narrative describes a completed past event, so the simple past "returned" is correct.

◦ "Their" is the possessive adjective (belonging to them) and is right before the noun desks; "there" refers to a place and would be meaningless here.

◦ Corrected sentence: After recess, the students returned to their desks.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "returned to there" fixes the verb but uses the wrong homophone.

• Option 2 "return to there" is wrong in both respects.

• Option 4 "No improvement" is wrong because the printed "returns" does not agree with the plural subject.

NOTE

• Homophone trio: their (possessive — their books), there (place — sit there), they're (they are).

• Note also the collocation "return to" a place: return to school, return to their desks — but return home takes no preposition.

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Allergies can indirect cause you to feel tired by robbing you of sleep.
option_4: cause you to feel tired by
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Allergies can indirect

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error is the use of the adjective "indirect" where an adverb is required.

◦ The word modifies the verb "cause" — it tells us how allergies cause tiredness — and verbs are modified by adverbs.

◦ The correct adverb is "indirectly".

◦ Corrected sentence: Allergies can indirectly cause you to feel tired by robbing you of sleep.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Segment "cause you to feel tired by" is correct — the structure "cause somebody to do something" takes the to-infinitive.

• Segment "robbing you of sleep." is correct — the preposition "by" is properly followed by the -ing form, and "rob somebody of something" is the standard collocation.

NOTE

• Remember: rob a person of a thing but steal a thing from a person — They robbed him of his watch / They stole his watch.

• Adjective → adverb: direct → directly, indirect → indirectly, quick → quickly, easy → easily.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.

Bonaparte, unlike Hoche, was not (eagerly to embark in) a serious Irish expedition.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. eager to embark on.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The bracketed segment contains two errors, and only Option 1 corrects both.

◦ After the linking verb "was not", an adjective is needed, not the adverb 'eagerly' — so "eager" is correct.

◦ The verb "embark" takes the preposition "on/upon" when it means to begin an important or difficult task: embark on a project / an expedition.

◦ Corrected sentence: Bonaparte, unlike Hoche, was not eager to embark on a serious Irish expedition.

◦ "Eager to + base verb" is the standard structure: eager to learn, eager to help.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "No substitution required" is wrong because of the adverb and preposition errors.

• Option 3 "eagerest to embarked on" is doubly wrong — the superlative of eager is most eager (never 'eagerest'), and 'embarked' cannot follow 'to'.

• Option 4 "eager into embark in" uses two wrong prepositions and no infinitive marker.

NOTE

• Note the two senses of embark: embark on a ship (to board) and embark on/upon a venture (to begin).

• Adjectives of two or more syllables form the comparative and superlative with more / most: more eager, most eager.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

You will ______ the price for this crime.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. pay.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed expression is "pay the price (for something)", which means to suffer the unpleasant consequences of one's actions. (कीमत चुकाना / भुगतना)

◦ Correct: You will pay the price for this crime.

◦ Example: He ignored every warning and is now paying the price for it.

◦ The related expression "pay the penalty" carries the same sense.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "make" does not collocate with 'the price'; one sets or fixes a price.

• Option 3 "pale" means to become pale in colour (a verb) or light in colour (an adjective).

• Option 4 "call" does not fit; "call the price" is not English in this sense.

NOTE

• Other collocations with pay: pay attention to, pay a visit, pay heed, pay respects, pay a compliment, pay off (to be worthwhile).

• Do not confuse pay the price (suffer consequences) with at any price (whatever the cost) and cheap at the price (worth the money).

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

The frequency of large wildfires ______ dramatically in recent decades.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. has increased.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject of the sentence is "The frequency" — a singular noun. The words "of large wildfires" form a prepositional phrase and do not change the number of the subject.

◦ A singular subject takes "has", so the correct present-perfect form is "has increased".

◦ The time expression "in recent decades" describes a period stretching from the past up to now, which is exactly when the present perfect is used.

◦ Correct: The frequency of large wildfires has increased dramatically in recent decades.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 4 "have increased" wrongly agrees with the nearby plural noun wildfires instead of the real subject — the classic trap in such questions.

• Option 3 "increase" is the plural present form and does not agree with the singular subject.

• Option 1 "did increase" is an emphatic simple past and does not suit the ongoing period "in recent decades".

NOTE

• Golden rule: the verb agrees with the head noun of the subject, never with a noun inside an intervening phrase — The box of chocolates was empty.

• Present-perfect signal words: since, for, so far, recently, in recent years/decades, already, yet, just.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Victorious
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Champion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Victorious" means having won a victory; triumphant. (विजयी)

◦ "Champion" refers to a winner — one who has defeated all rivals in a competition — and is therefore the closest in meaning among the options.

◦ Example: The victorious team returned home as national champions.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Unsuccessful", Option 3 "Failing" and Option 4 "Losing" are all antonyms of victorious — the examiner has filled the paper with opposites to test careful reading.

NOTE

• Synonyms of victorious: triumphant, winning, conquering, successful, champion.

• Antonyms of victorious: defeated, beaten, vanquished, unsuccessful, losing.

• Word family: victory (noun), victor (the winner), victorious (adjective), victoriously (adverb).

question:
The statement below has been given with bracketed text. Select the option with correct idiom for the bracketed text.

I'm sorry I snapped at you earlier, I think I (am just in a bad mood today).
option_4: got up on the wrong side of the bed
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. got up on the wrong side of the bed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "get up on the wrong side of the bed" means to be in a bad mood or irritable for the whole day for no clear reason. (सुबह से मूड ख़राब होना)

◦ The bracketed part "am just in a bad mood today" carries exactly this sense, and the speaker's apology for snapping confirms it.

◦ Correct: I'm sorry I snapped at you earlier, I think I got up on the wrong side of the bed.

◦ Origin: an old superstition held that leaving the bed on the left side would bring bad luck for the day.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "two wrongs don't make right" is a proverb meaning that a second wrong act does not correct the first.

• Option 2 "clam up" means to become silent and refuse to speak.

• Option 3 "dressed to the nines" means dressed very smartly and elegantly.

NOTE

• Other mood idioms: have a chip on one's shoulder (be resentful), fly off the handle (lose one's temper suddenly), in high spirits (cheerful), down in the dumps (depressed).

• "Snap at somebody" in the sentence means to speak sharply and angrily.

question: Four words are given, out of which only one word is spelt correctly. Choose the correctly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. KNOWLEDGE.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Knowledge" is correctly spelt — k-n-o-w-l-e-d-g-e, with a silent k at the beginning and -edge at the end.

◦ It means facts, information and skills acquired through experience or education. (ज्ञान)

◦ Word family: know (verb), knowledge (noun), knowledgeable (adjective).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "LIHGTNING" is wrong; the correct spelling is "LIGHTNING" (the flash in the sky) — note that lightening with an 'e' means making lighter.

• Option 3 "OCCASSION" is wrong; the correct spelling is "OCCASION" — double c, single s.

• Option 4 "MILLENIUM" is wrong; the correct spelling is "MILLENNIUM" — double l and double n (from Latin mille = thousand + annus = year).

NOTE

• Words with a silent k: know, knee, knife, knock, knot, knight, knuckle.

• Other double-letter traps: accommodation, embarrass, committee, possession, necessary, occurrence, harass.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

I'll see you in the meets next week.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. at the meeting.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Two corrections are needed, and only Option 1 makes both.

◦ The correct noun is "meeting" — an organised gathering of people. "Meets" is used mainly for sporting events (a swimming meet) and does not fit the sense here.

◦ The correct preposition for being present at an event is "at": at the meeting, at the party, at the conference.

◦ Corrected sentence: I'll see you at the meeting next week.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "No improvement" is wrong because "in the meets" is unidiomatic.

• Option 3 "of the meeting" shows possession and cannot express place.

• Option 4 "on the meeting" would mean about the meeting (as in a report on the meeting), not the place where the people will meet.

NOTE

• Prepositions of place with events: at a meeting/party/wedding; in a room/building/city; on a street/floor/page.

• Related collocations: hold / attend / chair / call / postpone a meeting.

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

Able to do many different things
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Versatile.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Versatile" means able to do many different things well; adaptable and having many uses. (बहुमुखी प्रतिभा वाला)

◦ Example: He is a versatile artist who sings, paints and acts equally well.

◦ It comes from the Latin versare = to turn — hence one who can turn easily from one task to another.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Monastery" = a building where monks live.

• Option 3 "Omnipotent" = all-powerful; having unlimited power (prefix omni- = all) — power, not variety of skills.

• Option 4 "Niche" = a small specialised segment of a market, or a recess in a wall.

NOTE

• Related omni- words: omnipresent (present everywhere), omniscient (knowing everything), omnivorous (eating both plants and flesh).

• A close phrase is the idiom "jack of all trades" — one who can do many kinds of work, though it often carries the tail "but master of none".

question:
Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word.

Anomaly
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Regularity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An "Anomaly" is something that deviates from the normal or expected pattern; an irregularity. (विसंगति / असंगति)

◦ Its direct antonym is "Regularity" — the state of being normal, usual and following a fixed pattern. (नियमितता)

◦ Example: The scientists could not explain the anomaly in the readings, which otherwise showed perfect regularity.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Omen" = a sign of something that is going to happen in the future.

• Option 2 "Tangible" = able to be touched; clear and definite.

• Option 4 "Tangent" = a straight line touching a curve at one point; the idiom go off on a tangent means to change subject suddenly.

NOTE

• Synonyms of anomaly: irregularity, aberration, deviation, oddity, abnormality, exception.

• Antonyms of anomaly: regularity, normality, conformity, uniformity, consistency.

• Word family: anomalous (adjective), anomaly (noun).

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Both men and women consider a variety of concerns when selecting there outfits.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. when selecting there outfits.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error is the word "there", which must be replaced by the possessive adjective "their".

◦ The sentence speaks of the outfits belonging to the men and women, so the possessive form is required: "their outfits".

◦ "There" is an adverb of place (Sit there) or an introductory word (There is a book), and it can never come before a noun to show possession.

◦ Corrected sentence: Both men and women consider a variety of concerns when selecting their outfits.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Segment "Both men and women" is correct — "both ... and" is the proper correlative pair and makes the subject plural.

• Segment "consider a variety of concerns" is correct — the plural verb consider agrees with the plural subject.

• Option 3 "No error" is wrong because of the homophone mistake.

NOTE

• The trio their / there / they're is one of the most frequently tested spelling traps in SSC exams.

• With "both ... and", the verb is always plural: Both he and she are coming.

question: Choose the sentence with no spelling error.
option_1: You will be here for seventy-two hours.
option_2: You will be heare for seventy-two hours.
option_3: You will be here for sventy-two hours.
option_4: You will be here for seventy-two huors.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. You will be here for seventy-two hours.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In Option 1 every word is spelt correctly — "here", "seventy-two" and "hours".

◦ Here = h-e-r-e, meaning in this place.

◦ Seventy = s-e-v-e-n-t-y; compound numbers from twenty-one to ninety-nine are written with a hyphen — seventy-two, thirty-five, ninety-nine.

◦ Hours = h-o-u-r-s, with a silent h in pronunciation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 — "heare" is wrong; the correct spelling is "here" (do not confuse it with hear, meaning to perceive sound).

• Option 3 — "sventy-two" is wrong; the correct spelling is "seventy-two".

• Option 4 — "huors" is wrong; the correct spelling is "hours".

NOTE

• Homophones to remember: here / hear, hour / our, their / there, peace / piece.

• Words with a silent h: hour, honest, honour, heir, ghost, rhyme — note that these take an as the article: an hour, an honest man.

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

It'd be really cool if you got / on the team, I've never seen you / played badminton, are you good?
option_2: on the team, I've never seen you
option_4: It'd be really cool if you got
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. played badminton, are you good?

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error lies in the verb form after the verb of perception "seen".

◦ Rule: verbs of perception — see, hear, watch, notice, feel — are followed by the bare infinitive (V1) or the -ing form, never by the past form.

◦ So "I've never seen you played badminton" must become "I've never seen you play badminton" (the whole action) or "...seen you playing badminton" (the action in progress).

◦ Corrected sentence: It'd be really cool if you got on the team, I've never seen you play badminton, are you good?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Segment "It'd be really cool if you got" is acceptable — the contraction It'd (It would) with the past form in the if-clause forms a normal Type 2 conditional.

• Segment "on the team, I've never seen you" is correct — American usage says on the team, and the present perfect with never is right.

NOTE

• Compare: I saw him cross the road (I saw the complete action) and I saw him crossing the road (I saw it in progress).

• In the passive, however, these verbs take the to-infinitive: He was seen to cross the road.

question:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.

Feat
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Accomplishment.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Feat" is an achievement that requires great courage, skill or strength. (उपलब्धि / कारनामा)

◦ "Accomplishment" means something difficult that has been achieved successfully, and is therefore the closest synonym.

◦ Example: Climbing Everest without oxygen is a remarkable feat (accomplishment).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Hallowed" = holy, sacred, greatly revered.

• Option 2 "Handsy" is an informal adjective meaning inclined to touch others inappropriately.

• Option 4 "Obligation" = a duty or something one is bound to do, which is a responsibility, not an achievement.

NOTE

• Synonyms of feat: achievement, accomplishment, exploit, attainment, triumph, deed.

• Do not confuse the homophones feat (an achievement) and feet (the plural of foot).

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

Planking is free and (1) ______ only a couple of minutes — no gym membership or special equipment (2) ______. Squatting, dead-lifting and pressing overhead without injury is hard to do without a strong (3) ______. "We need to keep our spine straight to do these (4) ______. Planking provides you with better core strength to be able to brace during these (5) ______," Lawton says.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. takes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage states a general fact about planking, so the simple present tense is required.

◦ The subject "Planking" is a singular gerund, so the verb must carry -s: "takes".

◦ The first verb in the sentence, "is" (Planking is free), is also present tense, so "takes" keeps the tense consistent.

◦ The collocation is "take + time": It takes only a couple of minutes.

◦ Correct: Planking is free and takes only a couple of minutes.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "taken" is a past participle and cannot stand alone as a finite verb.

• Option 2 "has taken" is present perfect, which would wrongly suggest a completed action rather than a permanent fact.

• Option 4 "took" is simple past and clashes with the present-tense "is".

NOTE

• The simple present is used for universal truths, habits and permanent situations: Water boils at 100°C.

• Verb forms: take – took – taken.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

Planking is free and (1) ______ only a couple of minutes — no gym membership or special equipment (2) ______. Squatting, dead-lifting and pressing overhead without injury is hard to do without a strong (3) ______. "We need to keep our spine straight to do these (4) ______. Planking provides you with better core strength to be able to brace during these (5) ______," Lawton says.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. required.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The clause is elliptical — "no gym membership or special equipment (is) required" — meaning none is needed.

◦ This supports the writer's point that planking is free and convenient: it costs nothing and needs no apparatus.

◦ "Required" means needed or necessary, and it is the standard word used with equipment and qualifications.

◦ Correct: ... no gym membership or special equipment required.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "registered" = officially recorded, which does not fit 'equipment'.

• Option 3 "catered" = provided food or services for, used with the preposition for/to.

• Option 4 "placed" = put in a position, meaningless here.

NOTE

• "No ... required" is a common elliptical construction in notices and advertisements: No experience required, No booking required.

• Word family: require (verb), requirement (noun), requisite (adjective/noun).

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

Planking is free and (1) ______ only a couple of minutes — no gym membership or special equipment (2) ______. Squatting, dead-lifting and pressing overhead without injury is hard to do without a strong (3) ______. "We need to keep our spine straight to do these (4) ______. Planking provides you with better core strength to be able to brace during these (5) ______," Lawton says.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. core.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In fitness, the "core" means the group of muscles around the trunk — the abdomen, back and pelvis — that stabilise the body.

◦ The passage says heavy movements such as squatting and dead-lifting are hard to do safely "without a strong ______", and the very next sentence confirms it: "Planking provides you with better core strength".

◦ Correct: ... is hard to do without a strong core.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "spot", Option 3 "space" and Option 4 "matter" have no connection with muscular strength and do not collocate with 'strong' in this sense.

NOTE

• Cloze technique: when the same idea is repeated later in the passage ("core strength"), that repetition is the strongest clue to the missing word.

• "Core" also means the central or most important part of something: the core of the problem, core subjects, the earth's core.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

Planking is free and (1) ______ only a couple of minutes — no gym membership or special equipment (2) ______. Squatting, dead-lifting and pressing overhead without injury is hard to do without a strong (3) ______. "We need to keep our spine straight to do these (4) ______. Planking provides you with better core strength to be able to brace during these (5) ______," Lawton says.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. exercises.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "these" refers back to the activities just listed — squatting, dead-lifting and pressing overhead — and all of them are exercises.

◦ Correct: "We need to keep our spine straight to do these exercises."

◦ The whole passage is about physical fitness, so 'exercises' is the natural noun.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "therapies" = treatments for an illness, not fitness movements.

• Option 3 "surgeries" = medical operations.

• Option 4 "mechanics" = the study of motion and forces, or the workings of something.

NOTE

• In cloze passages, a demonstrative such as these / those / such always points back to something already mentioned — locate that reference first.

• Fitness vocabulary worth knowing: squat, dead-lift, plank, brace, posture, stamina, flexibility.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

Planking is free and (1) ______ only a couple of minutes — no gym membership or special equipment (2) ______. Squatting, dead-lifting and pressing overhead without injury is hard to do without a strong (3) ______. "We need to keep our spine straight to do these (4) ______. Planking provides you with better core strength to be able to brace during these (5) ______," Lawton says.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. movements.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The expert is speaking about bracing the body while performing the exercises, and the general word for such physical actions is "movements".

◦ Correct: "Planking provides you with better core strength to be able to brace during these movements."

◦ Squatting, dead-lifting and pressing overhead are all movements of the body under load, so the word fits both the sense and the context.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "drives" would mean journeys by car or organised campaigns.

• Option 2 "competitions" and Option 4 "games" both refer to contests, whereas the passage is about individual exercise, not sport against others.

NOTE

• "Brace" here means to tighten the muscles in preparation for effort or impact.

• Note the useful preposition: "during + noun" (during these movements) versus "while + -ing" (while performing these movements).

question: Plasma is often called the ______ state of matter.
solution_text:
The correct answer is fourth.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Plasma is called the fourth state of matter, after the three common states — solid, liquid and gas.

• It consists of a highly ionised gas containing free electrons and positive ions, produced when a gas is heated to a very high temperature or subjected to a strong electric field.

◦ Because the charged particles move freely, plasma is an excellent conductor of electricity and responds strongly to magnetic fields.

◦ Plasma is the most abundant state of matter in the universe — the Sun and all the stars are made of plasma.

◦ Everyday examples: fluorescent tubes, neon signs, lightning, the aurora and welding arcs.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The fifth state of matter is the Bose-Einstein Condensate (BEC), predicted by Satyendra Nath Bose and Albert Einstein, formed at temperatures near absolute zero (–273.15°C or 0 K).

• The term "plasma" was coined by the American chemist Irving Langmuir in 1928.

NOTE

• In the Sun, energy is produced by nuclear fusion, in which hydrogen nuclei fuse to form helium in the plasma state.

• Change of state terms: melting, freezing, evaporation, condensation, sublimation (solid directly to gas — camphor, naphthalene, dry ice) and deposition.

question: निम्नलिखित में से अंतिम पल्लव राजा कौन थे?
solution_text:
The correct answer is अपराजितवर्मन (Aparajitavarman).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Aparajitavarman was the last ruler of the Pallava dynasty. He was defeated around 897 CE by the Chola king Aditya I, which brought Pallava rule to an end.

• The Pallavas ruled from Kanchipuram (Kanchi) in present-day Tamil Nadu, roughly from the 3rd to the 9th century CE.

• Important Pallava rulers:

◦ Simhavishnu – regarded as the founder of the line of great Pallava rulers.

◦ Mahendravarman I – a great patron of art; he wrote the Sanskrit play Mattavilasa Prahasana and began rock-cut cave temples; he was defeated by the Chalukya king Pulakeshin II.

◦ Narasimhavarman I (Mamalla) – he defeated Pulakeshin II and gave his name to Mamallapuram (Mahabalipuram), famous for its rathas (monolithic temples) and the Shore Temple; the Chinese pilgrim Hiuen Tsang visited Kanchi during his reign.

◦ Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha) – built the Kailasanatha temple at Kanchipuram and the Shore Temple at Mamallapuram.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (inscribed 1984).

• The Pallavas were great patrons of Dravidian temple architecture, which developed through the Mahendra, Mamalla, Rajasimha and Nandivarman styles.

NOTE

• The Pallavas were succeeded in the Tamil country by the Cholas under Vijayalaya and Aditya I.

• Contemporary dynasties: Chalukyas of Badami (Deccan) and Pandyas of Madurai.

question: In October 2022, ISRO chairman announced expected launch year of Chandrayaan 3 in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2023.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In October 2022, the ISRO Chairman, Shri S. Somanath, announced that Chandrayaan-3 was expected to be launched in 2023.

• Chandrayaan-3 was subsequently launched on 14 July 2023 from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota, using the LVM3 launch vehicle, and its lander Vikram made a soft landing near the lunar south pole on 23 August 2023.

◦ It consists of a lander (Vikram), a rover (Pragyan) and a propulsion module; unlike Chandrayaan-2, it carried no orbiter.

◦ India thereby became the fourth country to soft-land on the Moon (after the USSR, USA and China) and the first to land near the lunar south pole.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Chandrayaan-1 was launched in 2008 and confirmed the presence of water molecules on the Moon.

• Chandrayaan-2 was launched in 2019; its orbiter is still functioning, though the lander could not achieve a soft landing.

• Mangalyaan (Mars Orbiter Mission) was launched in 2013, making India the first country to reach Mars orbit in its first attempt.

NOTE

• ISRO was established in 1969 and is headquartered at Bengaluru; its founder is Dr. Vikram Sarabhai, called the Father of the Indian Space Programme.

• 23 August is now observed as National Space Day in India.

question: Which among the following festivals is thanksgiving festival, mainly celebrated in Goa?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ladainha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ladainha (also called Ladain) is a thanksgiving festival celebrated mainly in Goa.

◦ It is a Christian devotional practice in which families and neighbours gather to sing litanies and offer prayers of thanksgiving, often followed by a shared feast.

◦ It reflects Goa's Indo-Portuguese cultural heritage.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Hornbill Festival is the famous "Festival of Festivals" of Nagaland, held every year in December at Kisama near Kohima.

• Myoko is a festival of the Apatani tribe of Arunachal Pradesh, celebrated for prosperity and fertility.

• Bihula is a folk festival of Bihar, associated with the worship of Manasa, the snake goddess.

• Other festivals of Goa: Carnival (Carnaval), Shigmo (the spring festival), the Feast of St. Francis Xavier and Sao Joao.

NOTE

• Goa became India's 25th State on 30 May 1987; its capital is Panaji, and it is the smallest Indian state by area.

• Goa was liberated from Portuguese rule in 1961 through Operation Vijay.

question: Which city hosted the 2022 commonwealth games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Birmingham.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The XXII Commonwealth Games 2022 were held at Birmingham, England, from 28 July to 8 August 2022.

◦ The mascot was "Perry", a bull inspired by Perry Barr, and the motto was "Games for Everyone".

◦ India finished fourth in the medal tally with 61 medals — 22 gold, 16 silver and 23 bronze.

◦ Mirabai Chanu won India's first gold of these Games in weightlifting (women's 49 kg).

◦ Australia topped the medal tally.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Commonwealth Games are held every four years; the first edition was in 1930 at Hamilton, Canada, as the British Empire Games.

• India hosted the Commonwealth Games in 2010 at New Delhi, where it finished second in the medal tally.

• The 2026 Commonwealth Games were awarded to Glasgow, Scotland.

NOTE

• The Games are organised by the Commonwealth Games Federation (CGF), headquartered in London.

• Cricket (women's T20) made its Commonwealth Games debut at Birmingham 2022, where India won the silver medal.

question: Which among the following books released in 2021 was written by Amartya Sen?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Home in the World.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Home in the World: A Memoir" was written by the Nobel laureate economist Amartya Sen and released in 2021.

◦ The memoir traces his life from Dhaka and Santiniketan to Kolkata, Cambridge and beyond, and reflects on the idea of home and identity.

• Amartya Sen won the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences in 1998 for his contributions to welfare economics, and received the Bharat Ratna in 1999.

◦ His other well-known works: Poverty and Famines, Development as Freedom, The Argumentative Indian, The Idea of Justice and An Uncertain Glory (with Jean Drèze).

◦ He helped develop the Human Development Index (HDI) along with Mahbub ul Haq.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Will" is the memoir of the American actor Will Smith (2021).

• "Skill It, Kill It" was written by the fitness expert Ranveer Allahbadia.

• Other Indian-origin Nobel laureates: Rabindranath Tagore (Literature, 1913), C. V. Raman (Physics, 1930), Mother Teresa (Peace, 1979), Kailash Satyarthi (Peace, 2014) and Abhijit Banerjee (Economics, 2019).

NOTE

• The HDI, published in the Human Development Report of the UNDP, combines life expectancy, education and per capita income.

• The Economics Nobel is formally the Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel, instituted in 1968.

question: What is the study of interactions between a living organism and its environment?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ecology.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ecology" is the branch of biology that studies the interactions between living organisms and their environment, and among organisms themselves. (पारिस्थितिकी)

◦ The term was coined by the German biologist Ernst Haeckel in 1866, from the Greek oikos (house) and logos (study).

◦ Levels of ecological organisation: organism → population → community → ecosystem → biome → biosphere.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• An "Ecosystem" is a functional unit in which the biotic community interacts with the abiotic environment — it is a unit of study, not the study itself, which is why it is not the answer here.

• A "Biome" is a large regional community of plants and animals shaped by climate — for example tropical rainforest, desert, grassland, tundra and taiga.

• A "Biosphere Reserve" is a protected area with three zones — core, buffer and transition — meant to conserve biodiversity while allowing sustainable use.

NOTE

• India's first biosphere reserve was the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve (1986).

• Related terms: food chain, food web, trophic level, ecological pyramid and habitat (the natural home of an organism) versus niche (its functional role).

question: संगफाओ (Sangphao) आदिवासी नृत्य निम्नलिखित में से किस राज्य में किया जाता है?
solution_text:
The correct answer is नागालैंड (Nagaland).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sangphao is a tribal dance of Nagaland, performed by the Naga tribes of the state.

◦ Like most Naga dances, it is performed at festivals and community celebrations, accompanied by log drums, war cries and traditional costumes with feathered headgear.

• Other well-known dances of Nagaland: Chang Lo (Sua Lua), Zeliang, Modse, Rengma and Aaluyattu.

• The Hornbill Festival, called the "Festival of Festivals", is held every December at Kisama near Kohima, and showcases the culture of all the Naga tribes.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The capital of Nagaland is Kohima; the state was formed on 1 December 1963 and became the 16th State of India.

• Major Naga tribes: Angami, Ao, Konyak, Sema, Lotha, Chang, Rengma and Zeliang.

• Moatsu (Ao tribe) and Sekrenyi (Angami tribe) are important Naga festivals.

NOTE

• Folk dances of other states in the options: Garba/Dandiya (Gujarat), Ghoomar/Kalbelia (Rajasthan) and Chhau/Baul/Gambhira (West Bengal).

• Nagaland, Mizoram and Arunachal Pradesh enjoy special provisions under Articles 371A, 371G and 371H respectively.

question: Which continent of the world is referred to as a "Continent, Dedicated to Science"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Antarctica.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Antarctica is called a "continent dedicated to science" (also a continent for peace and science) because, under the Antarctic Treaty of 1959 (in force from 1961), it is reserved exclusively for peaceful purposes and scientific research.

◦ The Treaty bans military activity, nuclear tests and the disposal of radioactive waste, and it freezes all territorial claims.

◦ It has no permanent human population — only scientists living at research stations.

• Other facts about Antarctica:

◦ It is the coldest, driest and windiest continent, and is often called a cold desert; the lowest temperature on the earth was recorded at Vostok Station.

◦ It contains about 70% of the world's fresh water in the form of ice.

◦ The South Pole lies on this continent.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• India's research stations in Antarctica: Dakshin Gangotri (1983, now decommissioned), Maitri (1989) and Bharati (2012). India's Arctic station is Himadri (2008, Svalbard).

• India's Antarctic programme is run by the National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), Goa, and India passed the Antarctic Act in 2022.

NOTE

• The ozone hole was discovered over Antarctica; the Montreal Protocol (1987) was adopted to phase out ozone-depleting substances.

• Asia is the largest continent, Africa the second largest, and Australia the smallest.

question: In which of the following parts of the Indian constitution, Fundamental Rights are contained?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Part III.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Fundamental Rights are contained in Part III of the Constitution of India, covering Articles 12 to 35.

◦ Part III is often described as the "Magna Carta of India", and the idea was borrowed from the Constitution of the USA.

• The six Fundamental Rights available today:

◦ Right to Equality – Articles 14–18

◦ Right to Freedom – Articles 19–22

◦ Right against Exploitation – Articles 23–24

◦ Right to Freedom of Religion – Articles 25–28

◦ Cultural and Educational Rights – Articles 29–30

◦ Right to Constitutional Remedies – Articles 32–35

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Part I – The Union and its territory (Articles 1–4); Part II – Citizenship (Articles 5–11); Part IV – Directive Principles of State Policy (Articles 36–51); Part IVA – Fundamental Duties (Article 51A); Part V – The Union (Articles 52–151).

• The Right to Property was deleted from Part III by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978, and is now a legal right under Article 300A.

NOTE

• Article 32, called by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar the "heart and soul of the Constitution", allows a citizen to move the Supreme Court directly for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights.

• The Constitution originally had 395 Articles, 22 Parts and 8 Schedules; it now has around 470 Articles, 25 Parts and 12 Schedules.

question: Who was the Governor-General of India when Doctrine of Lapse was introduced in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Dalhousie.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Doctrine of Lapse was introduced by Lord Dalhousie, Governor-General of India from 1848 to 1856.

◦ Under this policy, if an Indian ruler died without a natural male heir, his state would "lapse" to the British, and adopted sons were not recognised as successors.

◦ States annexed under it include Satara (1848), Jaitpur and Sambalpur (1849), Udaipur (1852), Jhansi (1853) and Nagpur (1854).

◦ Awadh was annexed in 1856 on the different ground of alleged misgovernment.

◦ The policy caused deep resentment and became one of the major causes of the Revolt of 1857; Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi and Nana Sahib were among those directly affected.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other reforms of Lord Dalhousie: introduction of the railways (first line, Bombay to Thane, 1853), the telegraph, the postal system (Post Office Act, 1854), Wood's Despatch on education (1854) and the Widow Remarriage Act (passed 1856).

• Lord Cornwallis (1786–93) introduced the Permanent Settlement (1793); Lord Canning was the last Governor-General and the first Viceroy; Lord Mountbatten was the last Viceroy.

NOTE

• The Doctrine of Lapse was abandoned after 1857, and Queen Victoria's Proclamation of 1858 promised to respect the rights of Indian princes.

• Lord Wellesley had earlier used the Subsidiary Alliance to extend British control.

question: Presence of which phenomenon leads to weakening of trade winds in a region?
solution_text:
The correct answer is El Nino.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• El Niño is the periodic warming of the surface waters of the central and eastern Pacific Ocean off the coast of Peru and Ecuador.

◦ During an El Niño event, the trade winds weaken or even reverse, because the pressure difference across the Pacific is reduced.

◦ Normally the easterly trade winds push warm surface water towards the western Pacific; when they weaken, this warm water flows back eastwards.

◦ The name means "the little boy / Christ Child" in Spanish, since it is usually noticed around Christmas.

◦ In India, El Niño is generally associated with a weak monsoon and drought conditions.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• La Niña is the opposite phase — an abnormal cooling of the same waters with stronger trade winds, usually bringing a good monsoon to India.

• The combined ocean–atmosphere phenomenon is called ENSO (El Niño–Southern Oscillation); the Southern Oscillation is the see-saw of air pressure between Tahiti and Darwin.

• The Coriolis force, caused by the earth's rotation, deflects winds — to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere (Ferrel's Law) — but does not weaken them.

• Mango showers are pre-monsoon showers in Kerala and Karnataka that help the ripening of mangoes.

NOTE

• Other local pre-monsoon storms: Kalbaisakhi/Nor'westers (West Bengal), Bardoli Chheerha (Assam), Loo (hot dry wind of northern India) and Blossom shower (coffee, Karnataka).

• The Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) also strongly influences the Indian monsoon.

question: The mode of nutrition in which organisms make food themselves from simple substances is called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is autotrophic nutrition.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Autotrophic nutrition is the mode in which an organism prepares its own food from simple inorganic substances such as carbon dioxide and water. (स्वपोषी पोषण)

◦ The prefix auto- means self and troph means nourishment.

◦ Green plants, algae and cyanobacteria are autotrophs; they use chlorophyll and sunlight to carry out photosynthesis:

◦ 6CO₂ + 6H₂O --(sunlight, chlorophyll)--> C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂

◦ Autotrophs are called producers and form the first trophic level of every food chain.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Heterotrophic nutrition — the organism depends on others for food; it includes:

◦ Holozoic (ingesting solid food — humans, Amoeba), Saprotrophic/Saprophytic (feeding on dead and decaying matter — fungi, bacteria, mushroom) and Parasitic (living on or in a host — Cuscuta, tapeworm, lice).

• Insectivorous plants such as the pitcher plant and Venus flytrap are autotrophic but trap insects to obtain nitrogen.

NOTE

• Chemoautotrophs (certain bacteria) make food using chemical energy instead of sunlight.

• Photosynthesis mainly occurs in the chloroplasts of leaf cells; gases are exchanged through stomata.

question: निम्नलिखित में से किस मृदा में स्वतः-जुताई की विशेषता के कारण सबसे कम जुताई की आवश्यकता होती है?
solution_text:
The correct answer is काली मृदा (Black soil).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Black soil is known for the property of "self-ploughing" (स्वतः-जुताई), so it needs the least ploughing.

◦ It is made of very fine clayey material and swells and becomes sticky when wet, but develops deep, wide cracks on drying.

◦ These cracks allow air to circulate deep into the soil and effectively turn it over — hence the term self-ploughing.

• Other features of black soil:

◦ It is also called regur soil or "black cotton soil", because it is ideal for growing cotton.

◦ It is formed from weathered lava (basalt) of the Deccan Trap region.

◦ It is found mainly in Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Chhattisgarh, Andhra Pradesh and parts of Tamil Nadu.

◦ It is rich in calcium carbonate, magnesium, potash and lime, but poor in phosphorus, nitrogen and organic matter, and has a high moisture-retaining capacity.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Red soil develops on crystalline igneous rocks; its red colour comes from the diffusion of iron in it.

• Laterite soil forms in areas of high temperature and heavy rainfall with intense leaching; it is used for making bricks and suits tea, coffee and cashew.

• Peaty soil is found in areas of heavy rainfall and high humidity with a large accumulation of organic matter — as in Kerala (Kuttanad), coastal Odisha and West Bengal.

NOTE

• Alluvial soil is the most widespread and most fertile soil of India, covering the northern plains; it is divided into the older Bhangar and the newer Khadar.

• Soil classification in India is done by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR).

question: निम्नलिखित में से किसने विधवा पुनर्विवाह संघ (Widow Re-Marriage Association) की स्थापना की थी?
solution_text:
The correct answer is पंडित विष्णु शास्त्री (Pandit Vishnu Shastri).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Widow Re-Marriage Association was founded by Pandit Vishnu Shastri Pandit in 1861 in the Bombay Presidency.

◦ Its aim was to promote and popularise the remarriage of Hindu widows, a cause that faced strong social opposition at the time.

◦ He also wrote and campaigned extensively in Marathi in favour of widow remarriage.

• Background of the movement:

◦ Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was the leading champion of widow remarriage in Bengal; largely through his efforts, the Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act was passed in 1856 during the governor-generalship of Lord Dalhousie (enacted under Lord Canning).

◦ Dhondo Keshav Karve later founded a widows' home and India's first women's university (SNDT, 1916).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj (1828) and campaigned against Sati, which was abolished by Lord William Bentinck in 1829.

• Swami Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission (1897).

• Keshab Chandra Sen was a Brahmo leader who helped found the Prarthana Samaj (1867); the Native Marriage Act (Civil Marriage Act) of 1872 owed much to his efforts.

NOTE

• Important social legislation: Abolition of Sati (1829), Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act (1856), Age of Consent Act (1891) and the Sharda Act / Child Marriage Restraint Act (1929).

• Jyotiba Phule and Savitribai Phule worked for women's education and founded the Satyashodhak Samaj (1873).

question: ______ is a Hindustani classical musician who plays the bowed instrument, the sarangi.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pandit Ram Narayan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Ram Narayan was the legendary Hindustani classical musician who popularised the sarangi as a solo concert instrument.

◦ The sarangi is a bowed string instrument (a Tata Vadya), traditionally used to accompany vocal music; its tone is said to resemble the human voice.

◦ He was born in Udaipur, Rajasthan (1927) and was honoured with the Padma Shri (1976), Padma Bhushan (1991) and Padma Vibhushan (2005).

◦ Another renowned sarangi player is Ustad Sultan Khan.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Sandeep Das is a famous tabla player and a member of the Grammy-winning Silk Road Ensemble.

• Ustad Zakir Hussain is the celebrated tabla maestro, son of Ustad Alla Rakha.

• Pandit Shiv Kumar Sharma popularised the santoor, a hundred-stringed instrument of Jammu & Kashmir.

NOTE

• Classification of Indian instruments: Tata Vadya (string — sarangi, sitar, sarod, veena, violin), Sushira Vadya (wind — flute, shehnai), Avanaddha Vadya (membrane percussion — tabla, mridangam, pakhawaj) and Ghana Vadya (solid percussion — manjira, jaltarang).

• Other artist–instrument pairs: Hariprasad Chaurasia – flute; Amjad Ali Khan – sarod; Bismillah Khan – shehnai; Ravi Shankar – sitar.

question: Which among the following is the oldest joint stock bank in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Allahabad Bank.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Allahabad Bank, established on 24 April 1865 at Allahabad (Prayagraj), is regarded as the oldest joint stock bank in India.

◦ It was nationalised in 1969 along with 13 other major banks.

◦ In 2020 it was merged into the Indian Bank as part of the consolidation of public sector banks.

• A joint stock bank is a bank owned by shareholders, whose capital is divided into transferable shares.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The oldest bank still in existence in India is the State Bank of India, which traces its origin to the Bank of Calcutta (1806), later the Bank of Bengal; the three presidency banks merged in 1921 to form the Imperial Bank of India, which became SBI in 1955.

• Punjab National Bank (1894, Lahore) was the first Indian bank started wholly with Indian capital; Lala Lajpat Rai was associated with its founding.

• Bank of Baroda was founded in 1908 by Maharaja Sayajirao Gaekwad III.

NOTE

• The Reserve Bank of India was established on 1 April 1935 on the recommendation of the Hilton Young Commission and was nationalised on 1 January 1949.

• 14 banks were nationalised in 1969 and 6 more in 1980.

question: Chandragupta, was the first ruler of the Gupta dynasty to adopt the grand title of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is maharaj-adhiraja.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chandragupta I was the first Gupta ruler to assume the grand title "Maharajadhiraja" — meaning "the great king of kings" — which marked the rise of the Guptas from a small local power to an imperial dynasty.

◦ He ruled from about 319–320 CE, and the Gupta Era is believed to have begun in 319–320 CE, probably from his accession.

◦ He strengthened his position through a matrimonial alliance by marrying the Lichchhavi princess Kumaradevi; the Chandragupta I–Kumaradevi type of gold coins commemorate this.

◦ His predecessors Sri Gupta and Ghatotkacha had used only the modest title "Maharaja".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Devanampriya (Beloved of the Gods)" and "Piyadassi" were titles used by the Mauryan emperor Ashoka in his inscriptions.

• Samudragupta, son of Chandragupta I, is called the "Napoleon of India" (a title given by V. A. Smith); his conquests are recorded in the Allahabad Pillar Inscription (Prayag Prashasti) composed by Harisena.

• Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya) defeated the Shakas and took the title Shakari; the Chinese pilgrim Fa-Hien visited India in his reign.

NOTE

• The Gupta age (c. 320–550 CE) is called the "Golden Age of India"; Aryabhata, Varahamihira, Brahmagupta and Kalidasa belong to this period.

• The Guptas issued the largest number of gold coins, called dinaras.

question: Which Indian monument was the most visited monument by domestic tourists in financial year 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Taj Mahal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Taj Mahal at Agra was the most visited monument by domestic tourists in the financial year 2022, according to data of the Ministry of Tourism / Archaeological Survey of India.

• Facts about the Taj Mahal:

◦ It was built by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan between 1631 and 1653 in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal.

◦ It stands on the bank of the river Yamuna and is made of white marble brought from Makrana, Rajasthan.

◦ The chief architect is generally identified as Ustad Ahmad Lahauri.

◦ It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983 and is one of the New Seven Wonders of the World (2007).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Humayun's Tomb (Delhi, built by his widow Hamida Banu Begum/Bega Begum, 1570) is the first garden-tomb in the Indian subcontinent and inspired the design of the Taj Mahal; UNESCO site since 1993.

• The Red Fort Complex, built by Shah Jahan, became a UNESCO site in 2007; the Prime Minister hoists the national flag there on Independence Day.

• Qutub Minar, begun by Qutb-ud-din Aibak and completed by Iltutmish, is the tallest brick minaret in the world and a UNESCO site since 1993.

NOTE

• The Taj Mahal faces damage from air pollution, which causes "marble cancer" — yellowing of the marble by acid rain and suspended particulate matter.

• The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) was founded in 1861 by Alexander Cunningham, known as the Father of Indian Archaeology.

question: भारत की किस स्थापत्य शैली को लटकती बालकनियों और मेहराब के आकार की कंगनी (cornices) के उपयोग के कारण अलग पहचान मिली?
solution_text:
The correct answer is राजपूत (Rajput).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rajput architecture is distinguished by its use of hanging balconies (jharokhas) and arch-shaped cornices (bangaldar chhajjas).

◦ A jharokha is an overhanging enclosed balcony projecting from the wall, used both for ventilation and for viewing processions.

◦ Other typical features: chhatris (elevated dome-shaped pavilions), jaali (perforated stone screens), massive forts on hilltops and ornate palace complexes.

• Famous examples: the Hawa Mahal (Jaipur) with its 953 jharokhas, Amber Fort, City Palace (Udaipur), Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh, Mehrangarh (Jodhpur) and Jaisalmer Fort.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Hill Forts of Rajasthan — Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh, Ranthambore, Amber, Jaisalmer and Gagron — were inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2013.

• Sikh architecture is marked by fluted domes, multiple chhatris and extensive use of gilding, as in the Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib), Amritsar.

• Nagara is the North Indian temple style, characterised by the curvilinear shikhara; Dravida is the South Indian style with its pyramidal vimana and gopurams; Vesara is the hybrid style of the Deccan.

NOTE

• Mughal architecture is known for large domes, minarets, pietra dura (inlay) work, charbagh gardens and the use of red sandstone and white marble.

• The Rajput and Mughal styles influenced each other, producing the composite Indo-Islamic architecture of northern India.

question: Who was the only female Muslim ruler to ever rule India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Razia Sultan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Razia Sultan (Raziyya al-Din) was the only woman ever to sit on the throne of Delhi, ruling from 1236 to 1240.

◦ She was the daughter of Iltutmish, who nominated her as his successor in preference to his sons — a remarkable decision for the age.

◦ She belonged to the Slave (Mamluk) Dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate.

◦ She discarded the veil, wore male attire and held open court, which offended the Turkish nobility known as the "Chalisa" or Chahalgani (the Forty).

◦ She appointed Jalal-ud-din Yaqut, an Abyssinian, to a high post, which further angered the nobles; she was overthrown and killed in 1240.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Rabia-ud-Daurani was the title of Dilras Banu Begum, wife of Aurangzeb, for whom the Bibi ka Maqbara at Aurangabad was built.

• Hamida Banu Begum (Bega Begum) built Humayun's Tomb.

• Arjumand Banu Begum was the real name of Mumtaz Mahal, in whose memory the Taj Mahal was built.

NOTE

• Rulers of the Slave Dynasty (1206–1290): Qutb-ud-din Aibak (founder, built the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque and began the Qutub Minar), Iltutmish (introduced the silver tanka and copper jital), Razia Sultan and Balban (introduced Sijda and Paibos, and the theory of kingship).

• Other notable women rulers of India: Rani Durgavati, Chand Bibi, Ahilyabai Holkar and Rani Lakshmibai.

question: Who has been appointed as the new Chief Executive Officer of NITI Aayog in June 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Parameswaran Iyer.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Parameswaran Iyer, a former IAS officer, was appointed the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of NITI Aayog in June 2022, succeeding Amitabh Kant.

◦ He had earlier headed the Swachh Bharat Mission as Secretary, Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation.

• About NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India):

◦ It was established on 1 January 2015, replacing the Planning Commission (1950).

◦ It is a think tank / advisory body, not a constitutional or statutory body, and was set up by an executive resolution of the Union Cabinet.

◦ The Prime Minister is its Chairperson; it also has a Vice-Chairperson, full-time members, ex-officio members, special invitees and a CEO.

◦ Its Governing Council consists of all Chief Ministers and the Lieutenant Governors of Union Territories.

◦ Its guiding principle is "Cooperative and Competitive Federalism", and its motto is "Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Dr. P. K. Mishra is the Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister, and Ramesh Chand is a member of NITI Aayog specialising in agriculture.

• The first Vice-Chairman of NITI Aayog was Arvind Panagariya.

• NITI Aayog publishes the SDG India Index, the Multidimensional Poverty Index, the Health Index and School Education Quality Index.

NOTE

• The Planning Commission was set up in 1950 and the Five Year Plans ran from 1951 to 2017; the 12th Plan (2012–17) was the last.

• Atal Innovation Mission (AIM) and Aspirational Districts Programme are flagship initiatives run under NITI Aayog.

question: Who among the following revived Kuchipudi, started his own "Kuchipudi Dance Academy" in Chennai and received 'Padma Bhushan' in the year 1998?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Guru Vempati Chinna Satyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Guru Vempati Chinna Satyam (1929–2012) was the legendary dancer and teacher who revived and reshaped Kuchipudi as a major classical dance form.

◦ He founded the "Kuchipudi Art Academy" in Chennai (Madras) in 1963, training generations of dancers.

◦ He was honoured with the Padma Bhushan in 1998, and also received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

◦ He choreographed several famous dance-dramas, including Srinivasa Kalyanam and Padmavati Srinivasam.

• Kuchipudi is the classical dance of Andhra Pradesh, named after the village of Kuchipudi (Kuchelapuram) in Krishna district.

◦ It was systematised in the 17th century by Siddhendra Yogi, author of the dance-drama Bhama Kalapam.

◦ Its distinctive item is the Tarangam, in which the dancer performs on the rim of a brass plate, often balancing a pot of water on the head.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kelucharan Mohapatra was the doyen of Odissi; Guru Bipin Singh was the great teacher of Manipuri; Uday Shankar was the pioneer of modern/creative Indian dance.

• Other famous Kuchipudi exponents: Raja and Radha Reddy, Yamini Krishnamurthy and Shobha Naidu.

NOTE

• The eight classical dances: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (UP), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

• The order of civilian awards: Bharat Ratna > Padma Vibhushan > Padma Bhushan > Padma Shri.

question: In hockey, yellow card refers to temporary suspension of player for a minimum of ______ minutes of playing time.
solution_text:
The correct answer is five.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In field hockey, a yellow card means a temporary suspension of the player for a minimum of five minutes of playing time.

• The three cards used in hockey are:

◦ Green card – an official warning, which also carries a two-minute suspension.

◦ Yellow card – temporary suspension for a minimum of 5 minutes (the umpire may impose a longer period for a more serious offence).

◦ Red card – permanent exclusion from the match; the player takes no further part and cannot be replaced.

• The suspended player waits in the sin bin, and the team plays with one player fewer during that time.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Field hockey is played by 11 players per side, and the game is governed by the International Hockey Federation (FIH), headquartered at Lausanne, Switzerland.

• Hockey India governs the sport in India; the Dhyan Chand Award and National Sports Day (29 August) honour the legendary Major Dhyan Chand.

• Hockey terms: bully, penalty corner, penalty stroke, dribble, scoop, tackle, sin bin.

NOTE

• India has won 8 Olympic gold medals in men's hockey, the last in Moscow 1980; the team won bronze at Tokyo 2020.

• Important hockey trophies: Agha Khan Cup, Beighton Cup, Dhyan Chand Trophy, Rangaswami Cup and the Azlan Shah Cup.

question: जब व्यक्ति नए देश में जाता है, तो उसे ______ कहते हैं।
solution_text:
The correct answer is आप्रवास (Immigration).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Immigration (आप्रवास) means the movement of a person into a new country with the intention of settling there — that is, arrival from the point of view of the receiving country.

◦ The person who comes in is called an immigrant (आप्रवासी).

• Emigration (उत्प्रवास) is the opposite — the act of leaving one's own country to settle elsewhere; such a person is an emigrant.

◦ Easy way to remember: Immigration = coming In; Emigration = Exiting.

• Both terms apply to international migration, whereas in-migration and out-migration are used for movement within a country.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Migration is one of the three components of population change, along with births (natality) and deaths (mortality).

• Causes of migration are divided into push factors (poverty, unemployment, disasters, war) and pull factors (jobs, better wages, education, security).

• Streams of internal migration in India: rural-to-rural, rural-to-urban, urban-to-urban and urban-to-rural; rural-to-urban migration drives the growth of Indian cities.

NOTE

• As per Census 2011, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar were the largest sources of out-migrants, while Maharashtra and Delhi received the largest numbers.

• India receives the highest remittances in the world from its diaspora abroad.
